novelty_basis: Non-uniqueness of lexicographic prime factorisation (with an invariant number of factors) is due to Imrich; cited via arXiv:2407.02615 and the Handbook of Product Graphs. The specific minimal example was not looked up.
proof_check: by hand (both sides are two disjoint 4-cycles plus two isolated vertices); minimality by the exact census EXP-C14-04
statement:
2K1[C4 + K1] and (2K2 + K1)[2K1] are both isomorphic to 2C4 + 2K1; C4 + K1 and 2K2 + K1 are prime (order 5),
so 2C4 + 2K1 has two lexicographic factorisations with different multisets of prime factors. No such
collision occurs below order 10.
title: The lexicographic product has non-unique factorisation already at order 10 (different multisets of primes)
